st: Mix [[4 cups]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt in a big bowl. Stir the melted butter, egg yolk and warm water together, then pour into the flour.
Knead the dough for about 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions with [[1 tsp]] salt for 15 minutes until very soft and golden.
Add the ground beef, cumin and paprika. Cook, breaking up the meat, until fully browned and no pink remains, about 8 minutes. Cool the filling completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough out thin and cut eight 6-inch circles.
Put a few spoonfuls of filling on each circle, then top with 3 egg slices, 2 olive halves and a few raisins.
Brush the edges with water, fold the dough over, and press and crimp the edge closed with a fork.
Place on a lined baking sheet, brush with the beaten egg and bake for 25 minutes until deep golden.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm.
Put the chicken in a pot, cover with water, add [[1 tsp]] salt and simmer for 20 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Shred it and set aside.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 12 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, cumin and paprika. Cook until fully browned and no pink remains, about 8 minutes. Stir in the shredded chicken and season.
Spread the meat mixture in a baking dish. Top with sliced eggs, olives and raisins.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Blend the corn, basil, milk, butter and [[1 tsp]] salt into a thick, slightly chunky paste.
Cook the corn paste in a pot over medium heat, stirring, for 10 minutes until it thickens like soft mashed potatoes.
Spoon the corn paste over the meat and smooth the top. Sprinkle with [[2 tbsp]] sugar.
Bake for 30 minutes until bubbling and browned on top. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Put the beef, water, onion, garlic, salt and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the chicken and carrots and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin and corn. Simmer for 15 minutes more.
Stir in the rice and cook for 12 minutes until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Taste the broth and add salt if needed.
Serve each person a piece of meat, chicken, a potato, some pumpkin and corn in a big bowl of broth, topped with cilantro.
Dice the tomatoes and drain off extra juice. Drain the sauerkraut well.
Mash the avocados with the lemon juice and salt until mostly smooth but a little chunky.
Simmer the hot dogs in hot water for 5 minutes until heated through and steaming.
Lightly toast the buns in a dry pan or oven for 2 minutes.
Place a hot dog in each bun.
Top each with a spoonful of tomato, then sauerkraut, then a generous layer of mashed avocado.
Finish with a thick line of mayonnaise and mustard if you like. Serve right away.
Boil the pumpkin cubes in the water for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash the pumpkin until completely smooth. Let it cool for 10 minutes.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Add the pumpkin and melted butter and mix. Knead on a floured surface for 3 minutes into a soft dough, adding a little flour if sticky.
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick, cut into 3-inch rounds, and poke each with a fork so it does not puff too much.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rounds a few at a time for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, plain or with pebre.

ing: large, to line and cover the pot
st: This is the home-stove version of the earth-pit dish. Season the pork and chicken with salt and pepper.
Line the bottom of a very large heavy pot with half the cabbage leaves.
Layer in the pork, then the sausage, then the chicken. Add the potatoes and the wine or water.
Cover with the remaining cabbage leaves, put the lid on tight, and cook over medium-low heat for 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the flour, mashed potato and a pinch of salt into a dough. Shape into 8 flat cakes.
Place the dough cakes on top of the cabbage and cook 20 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the pork is 145°F (63°C).
Scatter the clams and mussels on top, cover, and steam 8 to 10 minutes until the shells open. Throw away any that stay closed.
Serve everything piled on a platter with some of the pot juices.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika.
Add the beef and cook until browned and no pink remains, about 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, pumpkin, broth and salt. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes until the vegetables are very soft.
Mash some of the potato and pumpkin right in the pot with a spoon to thicken the stew.
Stir in the corn and peas and simmer 5 minutes more. It should be thick, like a mash.
Fry the eggs in a little oil until the whites are set.
Serve the stew in bowls, each topped with a fried egg.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft, then add garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the beans and water or broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes.
Add the pumpkin and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add half the corn. Blend the other half with a splash of the broth in a blender and stir it in to thicken the stew.
Simmer 10 more minutes until the beans are fully tender and the stew is creamy.
Stir in the basil, taste, and adjust the salt. Serve hot, often with a side of pasta or rice.

ing: soaked in warm water, or use foil and parchment
st: Soak the dried husks in warm water for 30 minutes so they bend without tearing.
Melt half the butter in a pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Blend the corn, milk and cooked onion into a thick, slightly coarse paste.
Pour the paste into the pan, add the rest of the butter, basil, salt and sugar. Cook, stirring, for 8 minutes until thick. Let it cool a little.
Lay two husks overlapping, put [[1/3 cup]] of the corn mixture in the center, and fold the sides over the filling.
Fold the ends in to form a closed packet and tie with strips of husk or twine.
Steam the packets in a covered steamer over simmering water for 40 minutes, adding water if it runs low.
Rest 5 minutes, then unwrap and serve hot with a little sugar or salsa.

ing: seeded and minced, or to taste
st: Dice the tomatoes and onion as small as you can. Put the tomatoes in a bowl.
Soak the diced onion in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain well, to mellow its bite.
Chop the cilantro and mince the chili and garlic.
Add the cilantro, chili and garlic to the bowl with the tomatoes, then add the soaked onion.
Stir in the olive oil, vinegar, salt and water.
Let it sit for 15 minutes so the flavors blend, then taste and add more salt or chili. Serve with bread or grilled meat.
Cut the potatoes into fries, rinse in cold water, and dry well.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the potatoes in batches for 6 minutes until golden, drain and salt with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide skillet over high heat. Sear the beef strips for 3 minutes with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, then remove.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and sausage and cook for 8 minutes until the onions are soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Return the beef to the pan and toss for 1 minute to combine.
Fry the eggs in [[1 tbsp]] oil until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Pile the fries on a big platter, top with the beef and onion mixture, then finish with the fried eggs. Serve right away to share.
Rinse the dried peaches, put them in a bowl, cover with cold water and soak overnight or at least 4 hours.
Rinse the wheat, cover with water in a pot, and boil for 45 minutes until tender but still chewy. Drain and cool.
Drain the peaches and put them in a pot with [[4 cups]] water, the sugar, cinnamon sticks and orange peel.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 25 minutes until the peaches are soft and the liquid is a sweet amber syrup.
Remove the cinnamon and peel, then chill the peaches and syrup in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Put a few spoonfuls of cooked wheat in each tall glass, add 2 peaches, and pour the cold syrup over. Serve with a spoon.
Mix [[4 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] yeast and [[2 tsp]] salt, then add [[1.5 cup]] warm water and [[1 tbsp]] lard.
Knead 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces. Shape each into a small oval and let rest 15 minutes.
Take two ovals and press them together, then press a floured chopstick down the center to stick them tightly. This is the signature joint.
Place on a floured tray. Rise 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 450°F with a pan of hot water below.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes until the crust is golden and crackly. Break apart along the center to serve.
nt: Best swap: use shortening or oil in place of lard at the same amount.

st: Whisk the flour, cornstarch, baking powder and salt together in a bowl.
Beat the butter and powdered sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time.
Stir in the dry mix until a soft dough forms. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes so it is easy to roll.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Roll the dough 1/4 inch thick on a floured counter and cut 2 inch rounds.
Bake on lined trays for 12 minutes until set and barely golden at the edges. Cool fully on a rack.
Sandwich pairs of cookies with about [[1 tbsp]] manjar, pressing gently so it reaches the edges.
Melt the white chocolate gently in 20 second bursts in the microwave, stirring between each, until smooth.
Dip each sandwich halfway or fully in the chocolate, set on parchment and let it harden for 20 minutes.
nt: Baked at 350°F, then filled and dipped
Best swap: use dulce de leche from a can in place of manjar, 1 to 1.

ing: aji verde or green chile paste
st: Boil the green beans in salted water for 5 minutes until tender. Drain and cool under cold water.
Mash the avocado with [[1 tbsp]] aji verde and a pinch of salt for the green sauce.
Season the steak slices with salt on both sides.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over high heat until shimmering. Sear the steak for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned and no longer pink.
Split and toast the rolls lightly. Spread with mayonnaise on one side and the avocado mix on the other.
Layer steak, tomato slices and green beans in the roll. Press and serve warm.
nt: Best swap: use sliced portobello mushrooms in place of beef. Use jalapeno blended with avocado if you cannot find aji verde.
